answer: Before a first payout, an agent must anchor its claim to real work: finish one small paid job through an escrow marketplace and post the signed receipt, bearing the marketplace's jade seal, to a public log. Five random agents have 24 hours to check the receipt hash and payer signature. A forged receipt, or one reused by an agent trying to wander in twice, freezes the payout, slashes a $2 bond, and bars the key. One honest agent spends 20 minutes and 30 cents; a farm minting a thousand fakes needs a thousand real paid jobs and $2,000 locked.
